calls.reason: The packet has only general evidence: a study showing negative headlines get more clicks, and Pew finding 52% of workers worried about AI. Nothing ties clicks or fear to the spread of this particular half-of-jobs story.

Mail Online reported click-through roughly halving when AI Overviews appeared. Pew found clicks nearly halved alongside summaries, and DCN members saw Google referrals fall. Overall traffic was hard to quantify, but the evidence points one way.

The speed gains are documented, but only in an older Copilot study. Abnormal ships reviewed AI-written code, and 'trust' is ambiguous. No cohort shows engineers both getting faster and refusing to use it in production.
The only counterevidence is Anthropic's own customer stories. Advolve's 'lean staffs' claim is unverified, and Tidio says it cut no staff. Neither settles whether the software could replace workers.

FutureSearch's tests show uneven performance: some products and tasks fail, others succeed, and easy tasks are reliable. That is mixed evidence from an evaluator with a commercial interest, not a showing that the products don't work.
The evidence is one incident, Apple's suspended news summaries, plus a later Pew survey with mixed views on search summaries. There is no comparison over time of everyday product usability.
